title: Expose supplier-payment evidence in purchasing reconciliation workflows
description: Extend the existing Purchase Order and supplier invoice reconciliation workflows with read-only supplier-payment allocation evidence from ERP-049. Keep ordered, invoiced and payment-reference amounts distinct and do not calculate or claim an accounts-payable balance, settlement result, due date, aging bucket or tax position. Do not infer links, mutate source records, execute production SQL, deploy, or release.
acceptance_criteria: Purchase Order detail exposes active allocated supplier-payment evidence, allocation count and unallocated or unavailable context using only persisted ERP-049 allocation rows.
Purchase Order lists expose a bounded payment-evidence summary without issuing a database query per row.

The ERP-044 supplier invoice reconciliation report can display recorded payment-reference evidence alongside ordered and invoice-allocation evidence while keeping the three evidence classes in separate labeled fields.
Supplier and currency mismatches in historical evidence are displayed as invalid or unavailable and are never silently converted, merged or reassigned.
Voided allocation evidence is excluded from active totals but remains inspectable through an explicit historical status or detail view.
Missing payment allocation evidence is shown as none or unknown as appropriate and is never converted into unpaid, paid, overdue, settled or outstanding status.

The UI and documentation state that payment allocations are operational reference evidence, not confirmation of bank transfer, an accounts-payable ledger, a legal Supplier statement, payment authorization or settlement result.
The workflow is read-only and does not change Purchase Orders, invoices, payment documents, receipt progress, inventory cost, Supplier balances, expenses or tax records.
Queries are bounded or paged, avoid per-row database access and reuse ERP-044, ERP-048 and ERP-049 authoritative semantics rather than implementing a second reconciliation engine.

Unit/integration tests cover no evidence, partial and multiple allocations, void history, mismatched historical evidence, multiple Suppliers and currencies, bounded queries and source-record non-mutation; safe validation passes.
Browser/UI acceptance is recorded as deferred during development according to project policy.

scenarios: Open a Purchase Order with partial invoice and supplier-payment allocation evidence and verify ordered, invoiced and payment-reference values remain separately labeled and match their source registers.
Inspect an order with voided, mismatched or missing payment evidence and verify it is not presented as paid, settled, outstanding or overdue and that no source record changes.

human_gate.reason: Read-only presentation of repository payment-reference evidence. No real payment, production mutation, settlement, deployment or release is authorized.
